notes: AI 6 gains two sections: when to use a better prompt, retrieval, fine-tuning or distillation (with LoRA in one paragraph and fine-tuning data treated as a pipeline), how to choose a model, and guardrails in layers with red teaming as a test suite.
It also explains the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001 in a paragraph each, for the 'how would you get this past legal' question.
Four new exercises run in your browser with stand-in models: a fine-tuning dataset with a leak-proof split, an output guard, permission-aware retrieval and a red-team run with a canary secret.

Module A6 adds ML system design basics: the training pipeline, a model registry, batch or online inference, training-serving skew, drift, and how a new model is rolled out, with the fraud-detection interview answered step by step.
Two new exercises: a drift report with the population stability index, and a ship, stop or keep-running decision for an A/B test with a latency guardrail; plus three quiz and two interview questions.

New module O4, Running the data platform as a product, after O3: knowing the platform's users, service levels and error budgets with burn-rate alerts, on-call and incidents, cost showback and unit costs, adoption and outcome numbers instead of vanity ones, a scored roadmap and saying no, and funding and failure modes.

An architect's lens with six under-the-hood answers, and four exercises that run in your browser: decide page, ticket or nothing from an error budget's burn rate, show cost by team with the untagged share, score a backlog with RICE, and find the biggest drop in an adoption funnel.

A design problem (run a 12-person platform team for 40 teams as a product), ten quiz and seven interview questions, and twelve reels. If you started before this update, What is new lists it and nothing is marked done.
1289 of 1465 reels now play in the natural Heart voice.
